default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Noun-modifying clause qualifying the noun that follows (利用する人: people who use)
Recently, the number of people using convenience stores in Japan has increased.
Used to list representative examples, meaning "such as..."
Expresses a state resulting from an intentional action (おいてある: is placed / is kept on hand)
Potential form expressing ability or possibility (食べられる: can eat / can be eaten)
Convenience stores are convenient because they have items used in daily life such as soap, as well as vegetables, milk, and foods that can be eaten right away.
is placed, is kept on hand
Listing pattern meaning "both... and..." (おっともつまも: both husband and wife)
Expresses a change in state, meaning "to become..." (多くなりました: has increased / became more)
In Japan, there has been an increase in elderly people, people living alone, and households where both husband and wife work.
Used in comparisons meaning "rather than / instead of..." (買うより: rather than buying)
Offers advice or suggests a better choice, meaning "should... / had better..." (行ったほうがいい: should go)
Expresses a change in habit or state of mind, meaning "to come to... / to start doing..." (考えるようになった: started thinking that)
These people have come to think that rather than buying lots of cheap items at a distant supermarket, it is better to go to a store where they can easily buy only what they need.
came to (do), started to, reached the point of
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Way or method of doing an action (attached to the verb stem after dropping ます)
Everyone's way of working is different.
Asks for a choice between two alternatives: "which of A or B..."
Polite question ending expressing curiosity, wonder, or gentle inquiry
In a company, which type of person is needed: the go-getter type or the steady, persistent type?
Whenever / When... then... (expresses a natural or inevitable result)
To become, to turn into (expresses a change of state with い-adjectives: 明るい -> 明るくなる)
Because... / Since... (indicates a reason or cause)
When there are people who always smile and work hard energetically, the company becomes brighter, so the go-getter type is very important.
with all one's might, desperately, hard
to do one's best, to work hard, to persist
to be, to exist, to have (living things)
Even if..., even though... (expresses concession or contrast)
Only, just (limits the target or scope)
However, a company is an interesting place; even if only people of the same type gather, a good company cannot be made.
cannot be formed, cannot be made
Without doing V1, do V2 (indicates an accompanying action in the negative)
Must do, have to do (expresses an obligation or necessity)
Therefore, we must also value those who quietly and steadily work alone without saying anything.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: To... (used at the beginning of letters or notices to indicate the recipient)
＜To all members of the TF Baseball Team＞
Particle で indicates the location where an action or event takes place
The next practice will take place at Minami Sports Ground.
Minami Sports Ground is a sports ground in Noda City.
Because..., since... (indicates a cause or reason objectively and politely)
Please (do)... (used to politely ask or request someone to do something)
There are rules, so please pay attention.
使えません is the negative potential form of the verb 使う, expressing 'cannot use'.
On that day, the parking lot at the entrance of the sports ground cannot be used.
cannot use, cannot be used, unavailable
If/When... (sets up a hypothetical situation or condition)
Must not... / Do not... (used to state regulations, requirements, or prohibitions in notices)
If you come by car, please use a nearby coin parking lot (a parking lot for 200 yen per hour); do not park on nearby streets.
People in the neighborhood will be troubled.
to be troubled, to be inconvenienced, to face difficulty
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: Expresses capacity, status, or identity (as / in the role of ~).
Connects clauses to express an ongoing state (living in high mountains and...).
Pandas live deep in the high mountains of China and are known as rare animals whose fur is distinctly divided into white and black.
Indicates an action moving toward the speaker's location (came here, arrived).
Two of those pandas came to this zoo in April of last year.
Used with a negative verb to emphasize only a single item or action (only eat bamboo).
Indirect passive pattern: it is said that, supposedly ~.
Used to wonder to oneself or express a gentle question (I wonder...?).
It is said that pandas only eat bamboo, but I wonder what they are eating here.
to be said, said to be
Causative form (使役形): to feed, let or make someone/something eat.
Used to list representative items non-exhaustively (such as ~ and ~).
Hearsay pattern: I heard that ~ (relaying information heard).
At this zoo, they feed them 20kg to 30kg of bamboo a day, and I heard that they also feed them carrots, apples, and the like about 3 to 4 times.
and so on, etc., such as
to feed, let eat, make eat
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Indicates the ending point in time of an action (until the age of 60).
Nominalizes a verb using 「の」 to express that doing something is normal or common.
About 30 years ago, in Japan, it was normal for men to work at a single company until the age of 60.
to work for, be employed at
Lists representative actions (such as getting married, having children...).
Conditional / temporal pattern: after doing something... (after getting married or having children).
And back then, it was normal for women to quit their jobs after getting married or having children.
to quit, to stop, to leave
Concessive pattern: even if, even though... (even if the wife does not work).
Conditional pattern: if / as long as... (as long as there is money the husband brings home).
Used at the end of a sentence to explain a cause or reason (because...).
Because even if the wife did not work, as long as they had the money the husband received from the company, the whole family was able to live comfortably.
could do, was able to do
even if (one) does not do, even without doing
if there is, if one has
Expresses doing the subsequent action without doing the preceding action (living with peace of mind without worrying).
Expresses the speaker's personal thought or opinion (I think that...).
I think the era when a family could live with peace of mind without worrying about money was ① a very good era.
with peace of mind, feeling relieved
could do, was able to do
Provides an example or draws a comparison (e.g., like present times).
Compares two things (e.g., compared to the current era...).
Indicates a change of state for i-adjectives (to become..., e.g., become worse / fewer).
Compared to times like today, when Japan's economy has worsened, wages from work have decreased, or jobs are lost, I think that era was much better.
by far, much more, all along
Expresses a desire held continuously over a period of time in the past ('had been wanting to...').
For, to (from the standpoint of..., e.g., for women who wanted to work...).
Expresses conjecture or hearsay based on observation or report ('it seems that...', 'apparently').
However, ② back then, it seems to have been an unpleasant era for women who enjoyed working and wanted to work like men.
Indicates a gradual change or ongoing trend progressing from the past up to the present (e.g., gradually becoming impossible to make a living).
Even after... (e.g., continuing to work even after getting married).
Indicates a transition to a new habit, state, or routine ('to come to...', 'to start doing...').
Nowadays, since it has gradually become impossible to make a living on only the money the husband earns from work, women have come to continue working even after marriage.
gradually becoming unable to do, becoming impossible
Opposite to..., contrary to... (contrary to past thinking).
Indicates an ongoing process of change continuing and developing up to the present (e.g., an increasing number of people).
Then, this time, an increasing number of people have come to hold the opposite view from the past.
the past, old days, former times
Expresses two actions occurring simultaneously (e.g., raising children while pursuing other goals).
Expresses a desire for someone else to do something (wanting women to continue working).
Indicates a gradual change in state, habit, or mindset (gradually coming to think that...).

Young women have come to think that after getting married they want to stay at home, raising children while doing their best in areas outside of work, whereas young men have increasingly come to feel that because they help with housework, they want women to continue working all along.
want to do one's best, want to work hard
have come to be, have gradually become
if married, once married, after getting married
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Expresses past experience of having done something ("have done...").
Particle indicating a limit, destination, or extent ("all the way to...", "up to...").
Have you ever climbed all the way to the top of Mount Fuji?
Conjunction connecting two clauses, expressing continuation or a gentle contrast ("but / and").
Sentence pattern stating the existence of something at a specific location ("there is... at...").
Mount Fuji is 3,776 meters high, but there is a Shinto shrine there.
to exist, there is, to have
Clause directly modifying the following noun ("people who climbed Mt. Fuji").
Uses the て-form to connect actions in chronological sequence ("go to the shrine and pay respects").
People who climb Mount Fuji first go to the shrine to greet and pay respects to the deities.
first, first of all, to begin with
Expresses ability or conditions that permit doing an action ("can stay overnight").
Next to the shrine, there is a small building where people who climbed Mt. Fuji can stay overnight.
The particle は replaces が to emphasize the negative existence of something.
there is not, do not have
Particle used for a non-exhaustive listing of representative nouns ("such as... and...").
Expresses ability or permission to do something ("can eat").
In addition, you can eat dishes like curry or soba at the cafeteria.
Uses the particle も combined with the て-form to add another existing condition as a premise.
Indicates the ability to do something ("can buy souvenirs").
There is also a small shop, so you can buy souvenirs.
A set collocation expressing the action of sending a letter.
Expresses having the favorable circumstances or ability to do something ("can send a letter").
Additionally, there is also a post office, so you can send letters from there.
and then, after that, in addition
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Basic structure: The subject (は) performs an action (動詞) affecting the object (を).
Japanese people often eat boxed lunches (bento).
The particle 「の」 replaces 「が」 to mark the subject in a noun-modifying clause (おかあさんの作った弁当).
Used to list actions, states, or reasons of similar nature (not only... but also... / and...).
Particle meaning "also" or "too", used to link elements and emphasize similarity.
They eat boxed lunches made by their mothers, and they also eat bento from convenience stores.
Nominalizes a な-adjective using 「の」 combined with the topic particle 「は」: "The one/thing that is the most... is".
The most popular one is "ekiben" (train station bento).
train station bento, station boxed lunch
Sentence pattern used to define or explain the meaning of a word or concept: "... means / refers to...".
The particle 「を」 indicates the place or space through which a movement passes.
"Ekiben" refers to boxed lunches sold at a town's train station or inside trains running through that town.
train station bento, station boxed lunch
Explanatory pattern emphasizing a feature or reason: "The thing is that..." / "What is... is that...".
Used to describe features, shape, or appearance of something (here, having an interesting shape).
What distinguishes ekiben from convenience store bento is that it contains famous local dishes from that town, and the bento box itself has a very unique and interesting shape.
train station bento, station boxed lunch
having (a shape), taking the form of
Indicates a low degree with a negative predicate: "not that... / not particularly... / not so...".
Emphasizes exclusivity or limitation: "only... / nothing but... (no other option)".
Potential form of Group 1 verbs (買う -> 買える -> 買えません: cannot buy).
Of course, the price isn't that cheap, but you can only buy it in that town.
that much, so, to that extent
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: On Sunday, we will visit a sweets factory.
study tour, field trip, facility visit
Please gather at the west exit of Sakuragawa Station at 9:10.
Indicates purpose or a reminder: "Please do... so as not to... / in order not to...".
Please make sure to arrive on time so you won't be late.
not be late, not be delayed (nai-form of おくれる)
Expresses permission: It is fine to ~ / no problem to ~ (polite form: 〜てもかまいません).
Lists representative actions: Doing things like forgetting, losing, etc.
Indicates an objective, gentle cause or reason: Because..., since...
During the tour, taking photos is permitted, but please be careful because many people forget or lose their cameras.
study tour, field trip, facility visit
no problem, allowed, permitted, it's fine
Lists representative actions: Doing things like asking questions, taking notes, etc.
Expresses permission: It is fine to ~ / no problem doing ~.
Indicates the timing of an action: When/at the time of doing something...
You may ask questions or take notes, but please listen quietly when the explanation is being given.
doing (among other things), doing such things as
no problem, it is okay, not minding
Causative form combined with a receiving verb: To be allowed/permitted by someone to do something (here, being offered snacks to eat).
Indicates chronological order: After doing something...
A reminder or advice to make sure to do something: Please make sure to bring (it) back.
Also, after the tour, you will be offered snacks to eat, but please be sure to take any leftover snacks or trash home with you.
be allowed to eat, get to eat
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.3.s: Used after the recipient's name at the beginning of a letter or postcard, meaning 'to...'
Particle で combined with は to emphasize the setting or occasion ('at the...')
Thank you very much for the cherry blossom viewing last week.
Conjunction connecting sentences meaning 'but', or used as a soft introductory connector
Potential pattern expressing inability: 'cannot do V' (here: cannot forget)
It was my first time seeing Japanese cherry blossoms, and the blossoms at Ueno Park were so beautiful that I cannot forget them.
Indicates an objective, polite reason or cause: 'because...', 'since...'
Humble pattern (kenjougo) expressing a modest action performed by the speaker toward the listener
I also took a lot of photos, so I would like to send them to you if possible.
Pattern indicating that someone did something for the speaker with a feeling of gratitude
Noun-modifying clause: the clause '山本さんが作ってくれた' modifies the noun 'お弁当'
Also, the bento that Mr./Ms. Yamamoto made for me was very delicious.
Noun-forming pattern meaning 'way of doing V' or 'how to do V' (作り方 = how to make)
Polite request pattern: 'Could you please do V for me?'
The rolled omelet was especially delicious, so could you please teach me how to make it next time?
how to make, recipe, preparation method
to teach, to tell, to show
Sentence-ending particle used to seek agreement or confirmation from the listener: 'isn't it?', 'right?'
Next month's mountain climbing is something to look forward to as well, isn't it?
Expresses the speaker's intention or plan: 'intend to / plan to do V'
Tomorrow, I plan to borrow a mountain guidebook from the library.
If you have any recommended books, please let me know.
please tell me, please let me know
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Change of state for い-adjectives: 'to become...'
Difficulty in performing an action: 'hard to / difficult to (see)'
Indicates the time when an action occurs: 'when... / at the time of...'
When our eyesight gets worse and it becomes difficult to see things, we use glasses or contact lenses.
became difficult to see, became hard to see
Difficulty in performing an action: 'hard to / difficult to (see)'
Change into a state of ability: 'come to be able to / become able to (see)'
By doing so, things that are difficult to see become visible.
by doing so, in that way
hard to see, difficult to see
to be visible, can be seen
Listing multiple items: 'both N1 and N2...'
Indicates the target or perspective: 'for... / to...'
Both glasses and contact lenses are necessary items for people with poor eyesight.

First of all, since glasses are worn visibly, other people can clearly tell just by looking, but because contact lenses are placed inside the eyes, other people will not notice even if you are wearing them.
first, first of all, to begin with
even if wearing, even when wearing
cannot tell, not know, not notice
to understand, to tell, to recognize, to notice
Indicates a natural consequence or condition: 'whenever...', 'when...'
Listing representative actions: 'doing things like... and...'
In addition, when exercising, glasses can come off or fall off, making it difficult to exercise; contact lenses, however, rarely do that no matter how much you move, making it easy to exercise.
such a thing, that kind of thing
difficult to do, hard to do
even if (one) moves, no matter how much (one) moves
Expresses that something occasionally happens: 'there are times when...', 'sometimes...'
However, there are times when it can be dangerous.
Expresses regret or an unintentional action: 'end up doing...', 'accidentally...'
Explains a reason at the end of a sentence: 'because...', 'it is because...'
That is because if a ball hits an eye wearing a contact lens, it could result in an injury.
Lists representative actions: 'doing things like... and...'
Expresses an effort to form or maintain a habit: 'make an effort to...', 'make it a habit to...'
Considering the advantages of both, I make it a habit to use contact lenses when exercising, and wear glasses when studying or reading books.
